//: `exclude` REPLACES the base's list rather than merging with it, so the four
entries from expo/tsconfig.base are repeated here. Dropping one silently
puts that file back in the program.
`android` and `ios` matter because expo/tsconfig.base sets `allowJs: true`
and does not exclude them. A Gradle build writes generated JS under
and that bundle contains `process = this.process || {}`. TypeScript infers
that and merges it with the global `process`, which collapses `process.env`
to an object with no index signature. The only symptom is
`Property 'EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL' does not exist on type 'typeof env'` in
api/client.ts — a file nobody touched, failing because somebody ran
`npm run android`. Both directories are generated by `expo prebuild` and
gitignored, so nothing in them should ever be type-checked.
